title: Libellus Adversus Coelestium
author: Paulinus Mediolanensis
source: Translated by Claude from tmp367.tmp367.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.

passages.original: Quod si, ut caeteri auctores haereseos, qui jam dudum ab apostolica sede vel a patribus judicati, et extra sinum matris catholicae Ecclesiae effecti, per- petua morte b perierunt, etiam hi qui nunc depre- hensi sunt, vel deprehenduntur, in perfidia sua per- manent, spiritali gladio quo interimantur, tradantur : ut nunc Pelagius Coelestiusque, qui a beatae memo- riae praecessore tuae beatitudinis papa Innocentio, si rectam respuant fidem et in sua perversa doctrina perdurent, damnati sunt.
passages.english: But if, like the other authors of heresy who, long since judged by the apostolic see or by the fathers and put outside the bosom of mother catholic Church, have perished by perpetual death, these too who have now been detected, or are being detected, persist in their faithlessness, let them be handed over to the spiritual sword by which they may be slain: as now Pelagius and Caelestius [have been], who were condemned by the predecessor of your Beatitude, Pope Innocent of blessed memory, if they should reject the right faith and persist in their perverse doctrine.
passages.notes: The stray 'b' after 'perpetua morte' is taken as a footnote mark and omitted. The sentence is loosely constructed: 'Quod si' introduces a condition whose apodosis is the jussive 'tradantur', and the final clause about Pelagius and Caelestius is elliptical. The condemnation by Innocent was conditional on their refusing correction ('si rectam respuant fidem').
